name: Jean-Claude Trichet

summary.text: Jean-Claude Trichet was President of the European Central Bank from 2003 to 2011. Press reports in 2011 described him opposing a restructuring of Greek debt, arguing it could trigger a confidence crisis across the eurozone, and stating in June 2011 that the ECB was not in favour of restructuring and would reject private-sector involvement that was not voluntary.

facts.claim: Der Spiegel, as relayed by MNI in April 2011, reported that Trichet fiercely opposed a Greek restructuring in a finance ministers' telephone conference, arguing it could prompt a confidence crisis for the whole eurozone.
facts.quote: ECB president Jean-Claude Trichet, who also took part in the telephone conference, fiercely opposed a restructuring, arguing that it could prompt a confidence crisis for the whole Eurozone

facts.claim: In June 2011 Trichet said the ECB was 'not in favour of restructuring' and would reject private-sector involvement that was not voluntary.

facts.claim: Eichengreen and Wyplosz have argued that Trichet's objection was to Emergency Liquidity Assistance rather than to debt restructuring as such, given the ECB's mandate to lend only against good collateral.

sources.title: Must-read: Eichengreen and Wyplosz, 'How the Euro Crisis Was Successfully Resolved'
